description: Golden evaluation dataset for StudyAI enrichment pipeline baseline. 15 cases covering 8 categories.

eval_006.ref_rb_insert: RB insertion cases: uncle red → recolor; uncle black + triangle → rotate parent; uncle black + line → rotate grandparent.

eval_008.ref_optimization: Applications: finding extrema (f'=0, f'' test), related rates, curve sketching.

eval_010.ref_bloom_apps: Applications: avoiding disk reads in databases (Bigtable, Cassandra), cache filtering.

cases.subject: Computer Science
cases.input_note: Dijkstra's algorithm finds the shortest path from a source node to all other nodes in a weighted graph with non-negative edge weights. It uses a priority queue to greedily select the unvisited node with the smallest tentative distance.
expected_relevant_facts: Dijkstra finds shortest paths from a single source
Uses a priority queue for greedy selection
cases.reference_book_content: Dijkstra's algorithm time complexity is O((V + E) log V) with a binary heap. The algorithm maintains a set of visited nodes and a priority queue of unvisited nodes keyed by tentative distance. Proof of correctness uses the greedy choice property: when a node is extracted from the queue, its distance is final. Bellman-Ford handles negative weights but is slower at O(VE). A* adds a heuristic for faster single-target search.

cases.subject: Computer Science
cases.input_note: A hash table maps keys to values using a hash function. Collisions occur when different keys hash to the same index. Chaining resolves collisions by storing a linked list at each index. Open addressing resolves collisions by probing for the next available slot. Load factor α = n/m affects performance; rehashing when α > 0.75 keeps operations O(1) average.
expected_relevant_facts: Hash tables map keys to values via hash function
Collisions happen when keys map to same index
Chaining uses linked lists at each bucket
Open addressing probes for next slot
Rehash at α > 0.75 maintains O(1) average
cases.reference_book_content: Good hash functions distribute keys uniformly. Common probe sequences: linear (h(k)+i), quadratic (h(k)+i²), double hashing (h1(k)+i*h2(k)). Amortized analysis shows insert is O(1) despite occasional O(n) rehashing. Universal hashing provides probabilistic guarantees. Cuckoo hashing uses two tables for worst-case O(1) lookup. Consistent hashing minimizes reshuffling when table size changes.

cases.subject: Biology
cases.input_note: DNA polymerase synthesizes new DNA strands by adding nucleotides complementary to the template strand. It requires a primer with a free 3'-OH group to begin synthesis. The enzyme reads the template 3'→5' and synthesizes 5'→3'.
expected_relevant_facts: DNA polymerase adds nucleotides to 3' end
cases.reference_book_content: DNA polymerase has 3'→5' exonuclease proofreading activity that removes mismatched bases. On the leading strand, synthesis is continuous; on the lagging strand, Okazaki fragments are synthesized discontinuously. RNA primers are removed by RNase H or DNA pol I (in bacteria) and replaced with DNA. DNA ligase joins fragments. Telomerase adds repeats at chromosome ends.

cases.subject: Physics
cases.input_note: Newton's second law states F = ma. Force equals mass times acceleration. This explains how objects accelerate when forces are applied.

expected_gaps.topic: vector nature of force and acceleration

cases.reference_book_content: Force and acceleration are vectors; F = ma means net force vector equals mass times acceleration vector. Net force is the vector sum of all individual forces. The law holds only in inertial reference frames. More generally, F = dp/dt where p = mv is momentum. For constant mass, dp/dt = m(dv/dt) = ma. Impulse J = ∫F dt = Δp.

cases.subject: Chemistry
cases.input_note: Catalysts speed up reactions by lowering activation energy. They provide an alternative reaction pathway. Catalysts are not consumed in the reaction.
cases.reference_book_content: Homogeneous catalysts are in the same phase as reactants; heterogeneous are in a different phase (e.g., solid catalyst, gaseous reactants). Catalysts do not affect the equilibrium constant or position — they accelerate both forward and reverse reactions equally. Enzymes are protein catalysts with specific active sites. Catalyst poisoning occurs when impurities bind irreversibly to active sites. Turnover frequency measures catalytic activity.

cases.subject: Computer Science
cases.input_note: Binary search trees (BST) maintain the property that for any node, all keys in the left subtree are less than the node's key, and all keys in the right subtree are greater. Inorder traversal yields keys in sorted order. Search, insert, and delete take O(h) time where h is tree height. In the worst case (degenerate tree), h = n giving O(n). Balanced BSTs like AVL trees and Red-Black trees maintain h = O(log n) through rotations. AVL trees track balance factors (-1, 0, +1) and perform single or double rotations after insertions/deletions that violate balance. Red-Black trees use node colors (red/black) and five properties to guarantee h ≤ 2 log(n+1). Both achieve O(log n) worst-case for all operations.
expected_relevant_facts: AVL uses balance factors and rotations
cases.reference_book_content: AVL rotations: LL (right rotate), RR (left rotate), LR (left-right), RL (right-left). Red-Black properties: (1) nodes red/black, (2) root black, (3) leaves (NIL) black, (4) red node children black, (5) all paths from node to descendant leaves have same black-height. RB insertion cases: uncle red → recolor; uncle black + triangle → rotate parent; uncle black + line → rotate grandparent. B-trees are multiway trees for disk storage with high branching factor. Splay trees are self-adjusting with amortized O(log n).

cases.subject: Computer Science
cases.input_note: Dynamic programming solves problems by breaking them into overlapping subproblems and storing solutions to avoid recomputation. Two key properties: optimal substructure (optimal solution contains optimal subsolutions) and overlapping subproblems (same subproblems solved repeatedly). Memoization (top-down) caches recursive calls. Tabulation (bottom-up) fills a table iteratively. Classic examples: Fibonacci, Longest Common Subsequence, Knapsack, Edit Distance.
expected_relevant_facts: DP breaks problems into overlapping subproblems
Classic problems: Fibonacci, LCS, Knapsack, Edit Distance
cases.reference_book_content: Time complexity: O(number of subproblems × time per subproblem). Space can often be reduced (e.g., Fibonacci O(1) space, LCS O(min(m,n)) space). Reconstructing solutions requires storing choices or backtracking through table. Bitmask DP uses bitmasks to represent subsets (e.g., TSP O(n²2ⁿ)). DP on trees processes children bottom-up. Divide and conquer has non-overlapping subproblems. Greedy makes locally optimal choices without guaranteeing global optimum.

cases.subject: Mathematics
cases.input_note: The derivative of a function f at point x is the limit of the difference quotient: f'(x) = lim(h→0) (f(x+h) - f(x))/h. It represents the instantaneous rate of change and the slope of the tangent line.
expected_relevant_facts: Derivative definition: limit of difference quotient
cases.reference_book_content: Differentiation rules: power rule (xⁿ)' = nxⁿ⁻¹, product rule (fg)' = f'g + fg', quotient rule (f/g)' = (f'g - fg')/g², chain rule (f∘g)' = f'(g(x))·g'(x). Higher-order derivatives: f'', f''', f⁽ⁿ⁾. Applications: finding extrema (f'=0, f'' test), related rates, curve sketching. Mean Value Theorem: if f continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b), ∃c∈(a,b) with f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a). Integration is the inverse operation.

cases.subject: Economics
cases.input_note: Supply and demand determine market equilibrium price. When supply exceeds demand, prices fall. When demand exceeds supply, prices rise. At equilibrium, quantity supplied equals quantity demanded.
expected_relevant_facts: Supply and demand determine equilibrium price
cases.reference_book_content: Price elasticity of demand = %ΔQd / %ΔP. Elastic (|ε|>1), inelastic (|ε|<1), unit elastic (|ε|=1). Shifts in demand: income, preferences, related goods prices. Shifts in supply: input costs, technology, number of sellers. Consumer surplus = area below demand curve above price. Producer surplus = area above supply curve below price. Deadweight loss from taxes/price controls. First welfare theorem: competitive equilibrium is Pareto efficient.

cases.subject: Computer Science
cases.input_note: A Bloom filter is a probabilistic data structure for set membership tests. It uses k hash functions and a bit array of size m. To add an element, set bits at k hash positions. To test membership, check if all k bits are set. False positives possible (element not in set but all bits set), false negatives impossible. False positive rate ≈ (1 - e^(-kn/m))^k. Optimal k = (m/n) ln 2.
expected_relevant_facts: Bloom filter tests set membership probabilistically
Uses k hash functions and m-bit array
Add: set k bits; Test: check all k bits
False positives possible, false negatives impossible
cases.reference_book_content: Counting Bloom filters use counters instead of bits to support deletion. Scalable Bloom filters grow dynamically. Cuckoo filters use fingerprints and cuckoo hashing for better space efficiency and deletion support. Quotient filters store quotients of hashes for cache efficiency. Applications: avoiding disk reads in databases (Bigtable, Cassandra), cache filtering, network routing, spell checkers. HyperLogLog estimates cardinality, not membership.

cases.subject: Biology
cases.input_note: During cellular respiration, glucose is oxidized to produce ATP. Glycolysis breaks glucose into pyruvate in the cytoplasm, producing 2 ATP and 2 NADH. Pyruvate enters mitochondria for the citric acid cycle, producing more NADH and FADH₂. The electron transport chain uses these to create a proton gradient driving ATP synthase.
expected_relevant_facts: Citric acid cycle: pyruvate → CO₂ + NADH + FADH₂ (mitochondria)
ETC uses NADH/FADH₂ to create proton gradient
ATP synthase uses gradient to make ATP
cases.reference_book_content: Glycolysis regulated by phosphofructokinase-1 (PFK-1), inhibited by ATP/citrate, activated by AMP. Each NADH yields ~2.5 ATP, FADH₂ yields ~1.5 ATP via ETC. Without oxygen, fermentation regenerates NAD⁺ (lactic acid or ethanol). ETC complexes I-IV pump protons; complex V (ATP synthase) uses flow back. Reactive oxygen species (ROS) from electron leak cause oxidative damage. Uncoupling proteins dissipate gradient as heat.

cases.subject: Computer Science
cases.input_note: QuickSort is a divide-and-conquer sorting algorithm. It picks a pivot, partitions the array around the pivot, and recursively sorts the subarrays. Average case O(n log n), worst case O(n²).
expected_relevant_facts: Average O(n log n), worst O(n²)
cases.reference_book_content: Pivot strategies: first, last, median-of-three, random. Lomuto partition: simpler, more swaps; Hoare partition: fewer swaps, two pointers. Worst case: already sorted with first/last pivot. Randomized QuickSort picks random pivot → expected O(n log n). Space: O(log n) average (call stack), O(n) worst case. Introsort: switches to HeapSort when recursion depth exceeds 2 log n, guaranteeing O(n log n) worst case. Three-way partition handles duplicates efficiently (Dutch national flag).

cases.subject: Physics
cases.input_note: Entropy measures disorder in a system. The second law of thermodynamics states that entropy of an isolated system never decreases. ΔS ≥ 0 for any spontaneous process.
expected_relevant_facts: Second law: entropy of isolated system never decreases
cases.reference_book_content: Statistical entropy: S = k_B ln Ω where Ω = number of microstates. Information entropy: H = -Σ p log p (Shannon). Reversible process: ΔS = 0, system+surroundings unchanged. Irreversible: ΔS > 0. Gibbs free energy: G = H - TS, ΔG < 0 for spontaneous at constant T,P. Clausius inequality: ∮ δQ/T ≤ 0. Carnot efficiency: 1 - T_c/T_h. Third law: S → 0 as T → 0 for perfect crystal.

cases.subject: Computer Science
cases.input_note: Graph algorithms solve problems on networks of vertices and edges. Breadth-first search (BFS) explores level by level using a queue, finding shortest paths in unweighted graphs. Depth-first search (DFS) explores as far as possible using a stack/recursion, useful for topological sort and cycle detection. Dijkstra's algorithm finds shortest paths in weighted graphs with non-negative edges using a priority queue. Bellman-Ford handles negative weights but detects negative cycles. Floyd-Warshall computes all-pairs shortest paths in O(V³). Minimum spanning tree algorithms: Prim's (like Dijkstra) and Kruskal's (sort edges, union-find).
expected_relevant_facts: BFS: queue, level-order, shortest paths unweighted
DFS: stack/recursion, topological sort, cycle detection
Bellman-Ford: negative weights, detects negative cycles
Prim's MST: like Dijkstra, grows tree
cases.reference_book_content: A* uses heuristic h(n) for guided search; admissible if h(n) ≤ actual cost. Topological sort: Kahn's algorithm (BFS with indegree) or DFS post-order. Kosaraju's algorithm (two DFS passes) and Tarjan's algorithm (single DFS) find SCCs. Ford-Fulkerson with Edmonds-Karp (BFS) finds max flow in O(VE²). Push-relabel is faster. Adjacency list O(V+E) space, adjacency matrix O(V²). Incidence matrix for edge-centric algorithms. Graph coloring, Hamiltonian path are NP-complete.

cases.subject: Computer Science
cases.input_note: Operating system kernels manage hardware resources. Monolithic kernels run all services in kernel space (Linux). Microkernels run minimal services (IPC, scheduling, memory) in kernel space, others as user-space servers (MINIX, seL4). Hybrid kernels combine approaches (Windows NT, XNU). System calls transition user→kernel mode. Context switching saves/restores CPU state. Scheduling algorithms: round-robin, priority, CFS (Completely Fair Scheduler). Virtual memory uses page tables mapping virtual→physical addresses. Page faults trigger disk I/O. File systems: ext4 (journaling), ZFS (copy-on-write), FAT32 (legacy).
expected_relevant_facts: Monolithic: all services in kernel space (Linux)
Microkernel: minimal kernel, user-space servers (MINIX, seL4)
Virtual memory: page tables map virtual→physical
ext4: journaling, ZFS: copy-on-write, FAT32: legacy
cases.reference_book_content: Preemptive vs cooperative multitasking. Slab allocator caches kernel objects for fast allocation. I/O schedulers: noop, deadline, CFQ, BFQ. Capabilities are unforgeable tokens granting specific permissions; ACLs are lists per object. Namespaces isolate resources (PID, NET, MNT, UTS, IPC, USER); cgroups limit resource usage (CPU, memory, I/O). seccomp filters syscalls. KPTI mitigates Meltdown. eBPF runs sandboxed bytecode in kernel.
